analysis.title: Cooler US jobs growth supports a Federal Reserve pause in October
key_insights: September nonfarm payrolls rose +29k versus +90k consensus, with 60k of downward revisions to prior months.
Unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, driven by a partial recovery in the participation rate (61.8% from 61.6%) rather than layoffs.
Wage growth was 3% year-on-year versus 3.1% prior, which ING reads as no inflation threat from the jobs market.
ING says Fed leadership is leaning toward an October hold after comments from John Williams (NY Fed) and Philip Jefferson (Vice Chair) suggesting no urgency to hike.
A hot September CPI print (due 14 October) would be needed to make the October FOMC meeting interesting. ING's call for the next Fed hike is December.
ING believes market pricing of 3-4 Fed rate hikes is too aggressive.

Manufacturing jobs rose for a fourth consecutive month, with 72k added cumulatively since the start of the year. Advanced manufacturing (pharma, transport and aerospace, computing and electronics) is strongest.
Construction jobs also increased, potentially tied to data centre activity.
Services employment was weaker: information -10k, financial -7k, professional and business services -9k, government -17k.
The 'big 3' job-creating sectors since December 2022 remain private education and healthcare, state and local government, and leisure and hospitality.
The labour market is low hire, low fire. A low quits rate points to further downside risk to wage growth.
Unemployed people and job vacancies are now of similar number, versus two vacancies per unemployed American in early 2022.

sector_views.rationale: Fourth consecutive monthly rise in jobs, consistent with strong survey readings, led by advanced manufacturing.

tension_points.bull_case: Market pricing of 3-4 Fed hikes assumes persistent inflation pressure and a labour market firm enough to support tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: ING argues weak payrolls, rising unemployment, a low quits rate and 3% wage growth show no inflation threat from jobs, so pricing is too aggressive and an October hold is likely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot September CPI print, due 14 October, would put an October hike in play.
